title: Products and dimension growth of affine normal subgroups
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], closed and normal subgroup schemes as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme], and finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Affine means isomorphic to the spectrum of a commutative ring [def-pc-scheme]. Let $G$ be a separated finite-type $k$-group scheme, with no affineness or commutativity assumption. If $M,N\subseteq G$ are smooth connected affine closed normal subgroup schemes, there is a smooth connected affine closed normal subgroup scheme $P\subseteq G$ containing both, such that for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, an element $g\in G(R)$ belongs to $P(R)$ if and only if, after a faithfully flat finitely presented extension $R\to R'$, its restriction is a product $mn$ with $m\in M(R')$ and $n\in N(R')$. Here faithfully flat means that tensoring is exact and detects zero modules, and finitely presented means a quotient of a polynomial $R$-algebra in finitely many variables by a finitely generated ideal. Moreover the topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of closed subgroup schemes of $G$ are finite nonnegative integers bounded by $\dim G$, and for every strict closed inclusion $J\subsetneq K$ of smooth connected subgroup schemes of $G$ one has $\dim J<\dim K$.

source.place: Section 5(f), product as image of a semidirect product, printed pp.111--112; Proposition 8.1 (affine, smooth and connected extensions and quotients), printed p.149; Lemma 6.41 and greatest-dimension argument of Proposition 6.42, printed p.134. No Stacks tag states this algebraic-group product assertion. Proposition 1.35 and the dimension discussion, printed p.17, identify connected components with irreducible components; smoothness excludes a proper nilpotent thickening in the equal-dimension case.

proof.text: Normality of $M$ makes conjugation $N\times M\to M$ a morphism: on affine test schemes conjugation in $G$ factors through the closed subgroup $M$ by [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and the unique factorizations glue. On $D=M\times_kN$ define $(m,n)(m\prime,n\prime)=(m(nm\prime n^{-1}),nn\prime)$, unit $(1,1)$ and inverse $(n^{-1}m^{-1}n,n^{-1})$. The conjugation identity $(nn\prime)m(nn\prime)^{-1}=n(n\prime mn\prime^{-1})n^{-1}$ verifies associativity; the displayed inverse gives both inverse laws. Multiplication in $G$ gives a homomorphism $f:D\to G$, $f(m,n)=mn$, since $m(nm\prime n^{-1})nn\prime=mnm\prime n\prime$. If $M=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $N=\operatorname{Spec}B$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives $D=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kB)$; it is finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. It is separated: the diagonal of an affine scheme is induced by the surjective multiplication map on its coordinate tensor square, hence is a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Section 5(f), printed p.111: semidirect product and multiplication homomorphism.

proof.text: The second projection $r:D\to N$ is a homomorphism, has kernel $M\times\{1\}$, and has section $n\mapsto(1,n)$; in particular it is surjective. A $k$-basis of $A$ makes $A\otimes_kB$ a free $B$-module. Tensoring with a free module preserves exact sequences, so this is a flat ring map; [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] gives flatness of $r$. The kernel square follows on every test algebra by setting $n=1$, and its inclusion is closed by the affine quotient description in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Apply [lem-sfb-exact-algebraic-group-property-permanence] to $1\to M\to D\xrightarrow{r}N\to1$. Its hypotheses are now verified, and $M,N$ are smooth and connected by assumption. Thus $D$ is smooth and connected.

source.place: Section 5(f), p.111; Proposition 8.1(a), p.149, applied to the split extension.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization] to $f:D\to G$: both groups are separated and of finite type, without an affineness assumption on $G$. Obtain $D\xrightarrow{q}P\xrightarrow{j}G$ with $j$ a closed immersion and $q$ flat, surjective and finitely presented, having the same scheme-theoretic kernel $K$ as $f$. The lemma makes $K$ a closed normal subgroup of $D$ and $P$ a separated finite-type group scheme. The exact sequence $1\to K\to D\to P\to1$ and [lem-sfb-exact-algebraic-group-property-permanence] show that $P$ is affine, smooth and connected. No smoothness or connectedness of $K$ is used: only the quotient clauses of permanence are applied. The maps $m\mapsto q(m,1)$ and $n\mapsto q(1,n)$ factor the given inclusions of $M,N$ into $G$, so $P$ contains both.

source.place: Theorem 5.39, p.108; Section 5(f), p.111; Proposition 8.1(b), p.149.

proof.text: Write $P=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $D=\operatorname{Spec}E$. By [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra], $C,E$ are finite-type $k$-algebras. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0,k$), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $C$ Noetherian. The $k$-algebra generators of $E$ also generate it over $C$ through $q$, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] makes $C\to E$ finitely presented. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] it is flat; by surjectivity of $q$ and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat] it is faithfully flat. For $p\in P(R)$ put $R\prime=R\otimes_CE$. This extension is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change]. It is finitely presented: tensor a presentation $E=C[x_1,\ldots,x_t]/(h_1,\ldots,h_s)$ to obtain $R\prime=R[x_1,\ldots,x_t]/(h_1^R,\ldots,h_s^R)$. The canonical map $E\to R\prime$ is a point $(m,n)\in D(R\prime)=M(R\prime)\times N(R\prime)$ above $p$. Consequently $j(p)|_{R\prime}=mn$.

source.place: Section 5(f), p.111 and Proposition 5.46, p.110; finite-presentation refinement: Stacks Tag 00FP, algebra.tex, lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation.

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $g\in G(R)$ has $g|_{R\prime}=mn$ over a faithfully flat finitely presented extension $R\to R\prime$. The point $p\prime=q(m,n)$ of $P(R\prime)$ maps to $g|_{R\prime}$. On $R\prime\otimes_RR\prime$ its two restrictions are equal because their images under the closed immersion $j$ are both the restriction of $g$, and a closed immersion is injective on points of every test algebra by its surjective affine-ring description [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The single affine faithfully flat morphism $\operatorname{Spec}R\prime\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is fpqc: it is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine], surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum], and each affine open $V$ of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is quasi-compact and covered by principal opens of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ contained in $V$, so finitely many $D(a_i)$ suffice. Their inverse images $D(a_i)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R\prime$ are affine and their images cover $V$, as required by [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. The existence and uniqueness clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], applied to $P$ and to $G$, descend $p\prime$ to $p\in P(R)$ with $j(p)=g$. This proves both directions of the stated criterion.

source.place: Section 5(f), p.111; local-to-global membership: Stacks Tag 023Q, descent.tex, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms.

proof.text: For any $k$-algebra $R$, $h\in G(R)$ and $p\in P(R)$, step 4 supplies $R\to R\prime$ and $p|_{R\prime}=mn$ inside $G(R\prime)$. Then $hph^{-1}|_{R\prime}=(hmh^{-1})(hnh^{-1})$. Both factors lie respectively in $M(R\prime)$ and $N(R\prime)$ by their normality in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Step 5 gives $hph^{-1}\in P(R)$. Hence $P(R)$ is normal in $G(R)$ for every $R$, precisely normality of the subgroup scheme. This uses local membership, not the generally false identity $P(R)=M(R)N(R)$ without extending $R$.

source.place: Section 5(f), pp.111--112: product subgroup; normality checked on every algebra.

proof.text: By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], $\dim G$ is finite, with the chain convention of [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. A closed subgroup $H\hookrightarrow G$ has its underlying space homeomorphic to a closed subset by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Every chain of irreducible closed subsets in $H$ is therefore a chain in $G$, so $\dim H\le\dim G$. It is nonempty because the identity section maps $\operatorname{Spec}k$ into $H$, so it has a chain of length zero. Thus its dimension is a finite nonnegative integer, even if $H$ is nonreduced or disconnected.

source.place: Dimension discussion, printed p.17; finite-type finiteness is the existing dimension node; the closed-subset bound follows directly from chains.

proof.text: Let $J\subsetneq K$ be a strict closed inclusion of smooth connected subgroup schemes. As a closed subset of $G$, $K$ has finite dimension by step 7. Apply [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component] to $K$: connectedness makes its identity component all of $K$, so $|K|$ is irreducible. Smoothness over $k$ gives reducedness of $J$ and $K$ by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. If the support of $J$ were all of $K$, uniqueness of the reduced induced closed subscheme in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], applied to $J\hookrightarrow K$ and $\mathrm{id}_K$, would identify this inclusion with an isomorphism, contrary to strictness. Hence $|J|$ is a proper closed subset of $|K|$. Every irreducible closed chain in $|J|$ can be extended by the last term $|K|$, with a strict final inclusion. Therefore every length $r$ occurring in $J$ satisfies $r+1\le\dim K$. Since $J$ is nonempty and finite dimensional, its possible lengths have a maximum, giving $\dim J+1\le\dim K$, as required.

source.place: Corollary 1.35 and dimension discussion, p.17; greatest-dimension argument of Proposition 6.42, p.134; uniqueness of the reduced support: Stacks Tag 01J3, schemes.tex, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme.

I read the item, the new node and every cited statement against Milne iAG2017, using pdftotext of the literature copy. Sources: §5f (the image of N⋊H → G, quotient map, membership after a faithfully flat extension) and Prop 8.1, whose proof cites 1.62, 2.70, 5.29 and 5.59; I read all four. I also read Lemma 6.41, Prop 6.42 and Prop 8.2. The item statement is unchanged from the base. Step checks: step 1's semidirect law, inverses and homomorphism identity are correct, and D is affine, of finite type and separated. In step 2, r is flat because A⊗B is free over B, has kernel M×1, and the extension clause makes D smooth and connected. Step 3 uses the factorization node's real non-affine statement (flat surjective q, closed j, kernel K) and only the quotient clauses, so P is affine, smooth and connected without any assumption on the kernel. Step 4: E is finitely presented over the Noetherian C, and R⊗_C E is faithfully flat and finitely presented. Step 5: j is injective on points, the single map Spec R' → Spec R meets def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering via finitely many D(a_i), and representable descent gives j(p) = g. Step 6 gives normality by local membership. Step 7 bounds dim H ≤ dim G and gives dim H ≥ 0 from the identity section. Step 8: K is irreducible (identity-component node, k algebraically closed), J and K are reduced because smooth, and uniqueness of the reduced induced structure gives |J| ⊊ |K|, so a chain extends and dim J < dim K. Small cases: SL_2·G_m = GL_2, where R' is needed for an n-th root of det; M = N; G an abelian variety; α_p ⊂ G_a is excluded by smoothness. The new node is exactly Milne 8.1 with exactness written out, true (Frobenius/μ_p shows why the quotient clause needs no smooth kernel), and self-contained, statement-only and not a restatement of the item. Duplicate search: affine-normal-quotient-geometry (affine G only) and smooth-affine-normal-quotient-lifts (smooth kernel, constructive) are not duplicates. Batch 5: the newly cited factorization node reaches lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change, a mathlib leaf on base change of fppf coverings. That is a general fact outside the trace-formula and Poincaré-duality assumptions and their proofs, so it is not a reason to return. Tool uses for the maintainer to record: lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra, lem-kun-dimension-finite-type, sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced, lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme (general scheme facts). lean.statement: theorem affineNormalSubgroup_products {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) [IsSeparated G.X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.X.hom] [QuasiCompact G.X.hom] : (∀ (M N : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (iM : M ⟶ G) (iN : N ⟶ G) [IsClosedSubgroupScheme iM.hom.hom] [IsNormalSubgroupScheme iM.hom.hom] [IsClosedSubgroupScheme iN.hom.hom] [IsNormalSubgroupScheme iN.hom.hom] [Smooth M.X.hom] [ConnectedSpace M.X.left] [IsAffine M.X.left] [Smooth N.X.hom] [ConnectedSpace N.X.left] [IsAffine N.X.left], ∃ (P : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (iP : P ⟶ G), IsClosedSubgroupScheme iP.hom.hom ∧ IsNormalSubgroupScheme iP.hom.hom ∧ Smooth P.X.hom ∧ ConnectedSpace P.X.left ∧ IsAffine P.X.left ∧ (∃ a : M ⟶ P, a ≫ iP = iM) ∧ (∃ b : N ⟶ P, b ≫ iP = iN) ∧ ∀ (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] (g : Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k R))) ⟶ G.X), (∃ p : Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k R))) ⟶ P.X, p ≫ iP.hom.hom = g) ↔ ∃ (R' : Type u) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : Algebra k R') (φ : R →ₐ[k] R'), φ.toRingHom.FaithfullyFlat ∧ φ.toRingHom.FinitePresentation ∧ ∃ (m : Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k R'))) ⟶ M.X) (n : Over.mk (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k R'))) ⟶ N.X), Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom) ≫ g.left = ((m ≫ iM.hom.hom) * (n ≫ iN.hom.hom)).left) ∧ (∀ (H : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (i : H ⟶ G) [IsClosedSubgroupScheme i.hom.hom], ∃ d : ℕ, topologicalKrullDim H.X.left = (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ∧ (d : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDim G.X.left) ∧ (∀ (J K : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (iK : K ⟶ G) (j : J ⟶ K) [IsClosedSubgroupScheme iK.hom.hom] [IsClosedSubgroupScheme j.hom.hom] [Smooth J.X.hom] [ConnectedSpace J.X.left] [Smooth K.X.hom] [ConnectedSpace K.X.left], ¬ IsIso j.hom.hom.left → topologicalKrullDim J.X.left < topologicalKrullDim K.X.left)
